Supported syntax and dialect differences

All queries run locally using sql.js (SQLite compiled to WebAssembly). This is an introductory SQL practice sandbox. It is not Microsoft SQL Server, PostgreSQL or MySQL.

  • Practise SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, DISTINCT, joins, subqueries, common-table expressions, GROUP BY, HAVING, COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, ROUND, COALESCE, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, basic CREATE/ALTER/DROP TABLE, views and indexes supported by SQLite.
  • SQL Server mode adapts a whole-number TOP on one simple SELECT to a row limit, and removes an unquoted dbo. prefix. SQL Server/MySQL DROP INDEX ... ON table is adapted. PostgreSQL/MySQL use LIMIT. Literal strings and quoted names are not rewritten.
  • Generated IDs (IDENTITY, SERIAL, AUTO_INCREMENT), server administration, stored procedures, triggers, native date/string functions and transaction commands are not implemented. Use explicit primary-key values and native tools for those features.
  • SQLite does not reproduce native DBMS type, precision, string-length, collation, date, permission or optimiser behaviour. A query that runs here is not proof of identical behaviour on a native server. Use portable GROUP BY lists; the sandbox does not enforce every native grouping rule.
  • Each run is atomic: a failed batch is rolled back. Foreign keys are enabled. Results are capped at 500 rows per statement, queries time out after 4 seconds, and database pages are limited to about 32 MB. Stop/timeout reloads the demo. Avoid huge cross joins and recursive queries.
  • Each tab has its own in-memory database. Saved drafts still share the browser profile, so this is practice, not a private student account or secure assessment.
Native dialect reference (not all syntax runs in this browser)
Feature SQL Server PostgreSQL MySQL
First five rows SELECT TOP (5) ... ORDER BY ... ... ORDER BY ... LIMIT 5 ... ORDER BY ... LIMIT 5
Generated key INT IDENTITY(1,1) INTEGER GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY INT AUTO_INCREMENT
Identifier quoting [StudentName] "StudentName" `StudentName`
String concatenation CONCAT(a, b) a || b CONCAT(a, b)
Drop index DROP INDEX idx ON table_name DROP INDEX idx DROP INDEX idx ON table_name
